name: SQLflex
tagline: Low-cost Informix-SE and ESQL/C compatible SQL engine for Linux, UNIX, Windows and VMS from Infoflex.
description: SQLflex is Infoflex's clone of the Informix Standard Engine and the Informix ESQL/C API: the pitch is that existing Informix-SE applications and databases run unchanged at a fraction of IBM's price. It is a client/server ANSI SQL engine with row-level locking, unlimited users per runtime licence, a C API and script interface, and ports for Linux, UNIX, Windows and OpenVMS, sold alongside the company's Informix-compatible 4GL and accounting software. The product page and price list have not changed since at least 2006, so treat it as a niche migration target for old Informix-SE code rather than a modern database.
statusNote: Still listed on infoflex.com (site updated 2024), but the product page and pricing have been unchanged since at least 2006 with no visible releases.

pricing.notes: Per-CPU runtime licences, developer licences and a source-code licence; 15% annual maintenance.

strengths: Runs Informix-SE databases and ESQL/C code without changes
Much cheaper than IBM Informix licences, with unlimited users per runtime
Source-code licence available, and ports to OpenVMS and Linux
weaknesses: No visible development or releases in many years
Compatibility target is the old Informix-SE engine, not modern Informix
Very small vendor and user base
useCases: Keeping legacy Informix-SE and ESQL/C applications running cheaply
Moving Informix-SE apps off end-of-life hardware
notIdealFor: High concurrency or large data volumes
